ops.title: FP backend SHIPPED v0.39.0: local on FP, yasyf-home symlink-parked after the 07-05 migrate-storm wedge ([[fp-migrate-storm-incident]]); hard-won macOS platform facts — Settings toggle + one-time daemon TCC prompt, sandbox AF_UNIX rules, FPFS size-0 short-circuit, appex persists priv

ops.body:
**FP backend fully deployed on BOTH machines (2026-07-05, cc-pool v0.41.0):** local **12/12**
fileprovider (acct-06/11/12 auto-migrated by the daemon reconcile the instant the bridge bound
— symlink→FP is graceful even under a live session since no fuse mount is involved, so the
"migration kills the session" fear was unfounded) and **yasyf-home 10/10** fileprovider. No fuse
mounts remain anywhere. Loose ends: local **acct-09 needs `ccp login 9`** (server-REVOKED
refresh token from the July-3 meltdown — invalid_grant; no local copy recovers it, genuinely
interactive OAuth). fusekit fixes along the way: v0.29.1 (mux Teardown legacy arm), v0.29.2
(quarantine resolver), v0.30.0 (orphan reaping [[orphan-nfsv4-reaping]]).

**yasyf-home rollout facts (macOS 26.4.1):** (a) MUST `brew upgrade cc-pool` to v0.41.0 BEFORE
any migrate — the old resolver is the transcript-destroyer ([[overlay-conflict-resolver-data-loss]]).
(b) FP needed ZERO GUI there — the group-container bind succeeded with no consent prompt and the
provider was NOT user-disabled on a clean first-install (vs the local upgrade-reprompt path);
enablement asymmetry is per-machine/first-install-vs-upgrade. (c) **Reading an FP file over
plain ssh returns EDEADLK ("Resource deadlock avoided")** — File Provider materializes only in a
GUI/Aqua session context; the daemon (launchd gui/$UID) reads fine (identity verified at migrate,
zero content errors), and the user's sessions run via **Superset** which supplies GUI context, so
the ssh EDEADLK is a pure out-of-context artifact, NOT a serving failure. `launchctl asuser` over
ssh can't switch audit session to test it. (d) migration rolls back a row to symlink if the
drained account dir isn't empty — a leftover 0-byte `.claude.json.tmp.*` (or any unclassified
non-symlink file) blocks it; delete the litter and re-run `ccp migrate --account N --force`.

Platform facts that cost hours — trust these:
1. **Two separate enablement gates**: `pluginkit -e use` ('+' election) satisfies
   FileProviderAvailable, but fileproviderd separately holds the provider "⏹ user-disabled"
   (visible in `fileproviderctl dump <bundle-id>`) until the System Settings ▸ Login Items &
   Extensions ▸ File Providers toggle is flipped. **DEFINITIVELY no headless path** — proven in
   a SIP-off tahoe guest with the notarized build: the disabled flag lives in fileproviderd's
   private keyed store (absent from every defaults domain, plist, sqlite; `provision_tcc`'s
   TCC.db INSERT trick has no analog), survives a fileproviderd respawn, and no MDM/entitlement
   substitutes for a consumer Developer ID install. The Settings toggle is the ONLY consumer
   path. `ccp fp onboard` (v0.41.0) deep-links it and narrates. Running the FP VM scenarios
   therefore needs one manual GUI toggle → `tart clone` golden image (accepted tradeoff).
2. **The daemon's first bind in the App Group container blocks on a one-time TCC GUI prompt**
   (macOS 15+ group-container protection; entitled Developer ID CLI still prompts once). The
   bind HANGS silently until the user approves — looks like a wedge. The FP bridge serve loop
   retries with backoff + logs real errors precisely for this. **NOT permanent — the grant is
   cdhash-keyed, so EVERY version bump re-prompts** (proven 0.39.1→0.40.0→0.41.0), and under
   launchd the prompt never auto-surfaces. cc-pool v0.41.0 fixes the UX: daemon raises a precise
   `fp_consent_pending` Status flag (set only when the bind is genuinely parked / permission-
   denied, NOT on an unrelated bind error), doctor names the rung exactly, cask postflight
   relaunches the app (best-effort), and `ccp fp onboard` walks the whole flow. Closes f8e89e7.
3. **Sandboxed appex AF_UNIX rules**: file temp-exceptions (home-relative-path.read-write) do
   NOT cover connect(2) (network-outbound op); `network.client` covers REMOTE endpoints only —
   also insufficient. The group container is the only sanctioned socket location for
   appex↔daemon UDS. (Loopback TCP + token file was the fallback design, never needed.)
4. **FPFS satisfies a size-0 read WITHOUT calling fetchContents** — computed items must
   advertise their real byte length (appex does a bridge read per freshness-version, cached,
   "sz1:" version salt) or merged .claude.json/settings.json materialize EMPTY.
5. **The appex persists a committed .claude.json to the private backing itself** (mirrors the
   fuse holder's division of labor; Go WriteThrough only splits shareables to base). Without it
   private-key changes silently vanish on the next merge.
6. **Split has no deletion semantics**: removing a key through a domain write does not delete
   it from ~/.claude.json — clean base directly if needed.
7. fileproviderd redacts extension errors ("FP -1004 <private>"); the appex NSLogs enumeration
   failures (search `ccp-fp` in unified log). Poisoned domain enumeration state survives bridge
   recovery — re-register the domain (remove+register via ~/.cc-pool/domains.sock) to reset.
8. **Recovery goldmine**: every account keeps claude's own config backups at
   `acct-NN.private/backups/.claude.json.backup.*` (dotfiles — ls -a!). Restoring the newest
   into priv + signalEnumerator resurrects a stubbed account. Used to recover 6 accounts after
   the [[holder-bg-band-incident]] holder crash.

Cert/signing: Developer ID imported from 1Password OpenClaw (Stage 0); local FP builds signed
with team SXKCTF23Q2, `security import -T /usr/bin/codesign` avoided partition-list prompts.
Related: [[fusekit-content-over-rpc]], [[cc-pool-fileprovider-signing-reality]],
[[claude-pool-project]].
